question: According to which of the following foreign travellers, people of Delhi used to write letters containing abuses to the Sultan, therefore, in order to punish them Sultan decided to shift the capital?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ibn Batuta**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ibn Batuta visited India during the reign of Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
 
• According to his accounts, the people of Delhi used to write letters containing abuses to the Sultan.
 
• To punish them, the Sultan decided to shift the capital from Delhi to Devagiri, which he renamed as Daulatabad.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Hasan Nizami:
 
 
• Hasan Nizami was a Persian historian and writer during the medieval period.
 
• He is best known for his work, "Taj-ul-Maasir", a historical account of the reign of the Sultan of Delhi, Mahmud of Ghazni.
 
• Nizami's work offers valuable insights into the politics, culture, and social conditions of that period.
 
 
 
• Al-Biruni:
 
 
• Abu Rayhan al-Biruni (973–1048) was a renowned Persian scholar, historian, and polymath during the Islamic Golden Age.
 
• He made significant contributions to many fields, including astronomy, mathematics, physics, and geography.
 
• Al-Biruni is especially famous for his works on India, including "Kitab al-Hind", in which he detailed the culture, religion, and sciences of India.
 
• His scholarly approach combined a deep understanding of Indian civilization with a critical and comparative analysis.
 
 
 
• Isami:
 
 
• Isami (also known as Siyah-yi Isami) was a Persian historian and author who lived during the 14th century.
 
• He is best known for his historical work "Futuh al-Salatin" (The Conquests of Kings), which provides an account of the history of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• His work is a valuable source for understanding the history of medieval India, particularly during the reign of the early Sultans
